title: A router that says 404 vs 405 correctly
prompt:
Implement `Router` with `add(method, path, handler)` and `dispatch(method, path)`:

- paths are `/`-separated segments; a segment like `'{id}'` matches exactly one segment of any value and binds it as a string param
- `dispatch` returns `handler(params)` where params is a dict (empty for static routes)
- if some pattern matches the path with a DIFFERENT method → raise `RouterError(405, ...)`
- if no pattern matches the path at all → raise `RouterError(404, ...)`
- `RouterError` carries `.status`

tests.name: static routes, params, and binding
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add('GET', '/users/{id}', lambda p: f"user:{p['id']}")
r.add('GET', '/health', lambda p: 'ok')
assert r.dispatch('GET', '/users/42') == 'user:42'
assert r.dispatch('GET', '/health') == 'ok'
print('ok')
tests.hint: Split into segments; a {param} segment matches anything and binds it.

tests.name: 405 vs 404 are different diagnoses
tests.hint: Path matched but method didn't → 405. No pattern matched → 404.
